name: Egg Biryani
cuisine: Hyderabadi / Mughlai-style dum biryani (made across India; a staple of Mumbai biryani chains and delivery menus)
equipment: Small saucepan with a lid (for boiling the eggs and, separately, the rice)
Small heavy-bottomed pan or kadai (about 18 cm) with a tight lid, for the masala and dum
Tawa or flat pan to sit under the dum pan
Sieve or colander for draining the rice
Chopping board and knife; spoon; small bowls; measuring spoons; kitchen scale (cups and spoons are given for the scale-less)

steps.title: Wash the rice
steps.text: Put 70 g basmati in a bowl, cover with cold water, swirl and pour off; repeat 3 times.
steps.visualCue: The water turns from milky to almost clear
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Water swirled through rice and poured off.
steps.watchOut: Breaking the grains by rubbing hard; swirl gently with your fingers instead, since broken grains turn mushy later.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Cover the rice with fresh water (about 200 ml) and leave it.
steps.visualCue: Grains turn from translucent to chalky white and look slightly longer
steps.videoShot: Rice in water, timer set.
steps.watchOut: Soaking much longer than 30 min, which makes the grains fragile; set a timer.

steps.title: Start the eggs
steps.text: Put 2 eggs in the small saucepan, cover with cold water by 2 cm and bring to a gentle boil on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles first, then a steady rolling boil
steps.videoShot: Eggs in a pan of water coming to the boil.
steps.watchOut: Dropping cold eggs into boiling water, which cracks the shell; start them in cold water.

steps.title: Simmer the eggs
steps.text: Lower the heat so the water bubbles gently and cook for 9 min.
steps.visualCue: A gently bubbling surface, shells intact
steps.videoShot: Eggs bubbling gently with a timer on screen.
steps.watchOut: Boiling hard for too long; a grey-green ring around the yolk and a rubbery white show overcooking.

steps.title: Cool the eggs
steps.text: Move the eggs to a bowl of cold water for 3 min, then peel them.
steps.visualCue: Shell cracks and slips off in large pieces; the white is smooth and firm
steps.videoShot: A shell peeled off a boiled egg.
steps.watchOut: Peeling while hot, which tears the white; if the shell sticks, peel under running water.

steps.title: Slit the eggs
steps.text: Cut 3 shallow slits (about 3 mm deep) along each egg with a sharp knife, then pat dry.
steps.tip: The slits let spice get into the egg.
steps.visualCue: Thin cuts in the white that show the yolk does not break
steps.videoShot: A knife scoring a boiled egg.
steps.watchOut: Cutting deep, which splits the egg; slit only the white.

steps.title: Slice the onion
steps.text: Slice 80 g onion (1 small) into thin half-moons.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even slices about the thickness of a coin edge
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing an onion.
steps.watchOut: Uneven thick and thin slices, which brown unevenly; slice the same thickness.

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Chop 60 g tomato (½ medium) into small pieces.
steps.visualCue: Small pieces with the juice
steps.videoShot: A tomato being diced.
steps.watchOut: Leaving large chunks, which stay raw-tasting in the short cooking time; chop small.

steps.title: Make the ginger-garlic and chilli
steps.text: Mince 4 g ginger and 4 g garlic fine and slit 1 green chilli lengthways.
steps.visualCue: A coarse wet paste; chilli opened but still joined at the stem
steps.videoShot: Garlic crushed under a knife.
steps.watchOut: Garlic chopped too coarsely, which leaves a raw bite; mince until almost a paste.

steps.title: Chop the herbs
steps.text: Roughly chop 5 g mint and 5 g coriander leaves and put them together in a small bowl.
steps.visualCue: Fresh green, fragrant leaves, not bruised or wilted
steps.videoShot: A knife through mint and coriander.
steps.watchOut: Chopping too fine and early, which turns the herbs dark; roughly chop them just before layering if you can.

steps.title: Make the curd mix
steps.text: In a bowl, whisk 40 g curd with ¼ tsp (0.5 g) turmeric, ¾ tsp (2 g) red chilli powder, ¾ tsp (2 g) coriander powder and 2.5 g salt.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, evenly orange-red paste with no dry specks
steps.videoShot: Powders whisked into curd.
steps.watchOut: Lumps of dry powder, which burn later; whisk until completely smooth.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Heat 3 g oil (½ tsp) in the heavy pan on medium heat, add the eggs and a pinch of chilli powder and turmeric, and turn them for about 1–2 min.
steps.tip: Take them out onto a plate; they go back in at step 20.
steps.visualCue: The surface blisters and turns golden-orange; a spicy smell
steps.cameraCheck: The golden eggs in the pan
steps.videoShot: Eggs turned in oil until golden and blistered.
steps.watchOut: The spices burning in the dry spots of the pan, which turns them bitter and brown-black; keep the eggs moving and lift the pan off the heat if it smokes.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: In the same pan on medium heat, add 7 g oil (about 1½ tsp).
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmers
steps.videoShot: Oil swirled in the pan.
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil, which means it is too hot; lower the heat for a moment.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add 1 g cumin seeds, 1 cm cinnamon, 1 clove and 1 crushed cardamom pod and stir for 20 seconds.
steps.visualCue: Cumin sizzles and turns darker; a sweet, warm smell
steps.videoShot: Whole spices hitting hot oil.
steps.watchOut: Blackened spices, which taste bitter; if they blacken, discard and start again with a few new ones.

steps.title: Brown the onion
steps.text: Add the 80 g sliced onion and cook, stirring every minute.
steps.tip: Don't rush; browned onion gives the biryani its sweetness and colour.
steps.visualCue: Soft and translucent first, then light golden-brown at the edges with a sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The golden onion in the pan
steps.videoShot: Onion slowly turning golden.
steps.watchOut: Dark, bitter, burnt edges when the heat is too high; lower the heat and add 1 tbsp water to rescue it.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Stir in the ginger-garlic and the slit chilli.
steps.visualCue: The raw garlic smell goes and the mixture sizzles
steps.videoShot: Ginger-garlic stirred into onion.
steps.watchOut: Garlic browning, which turns it bitter; stir constantly for this minute.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and cook, mashing it with the spoon.
steps.visualCue: Tomato breaks down to a thick paste and oil starts to show at the edges
steps.videoShot: Tomato mashed into a paste.
steps.watchOut: Sour, watery masala from stopping too early; keep cooking until it is a thick paste with no pooled water.

steps.title: Add the curd mix
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the curd mix and 30 ml water, and stir for about 2 min.
steps.visualCue: A deep orange-red gravy that is thick and holds a spoon trail; the raw powder smell is gone
steps.cameraCheck: The finished masala in the pan
steps.videoShot: Curd mix stirred into the masala.
steps.watchOut: The curd splitting into grainy curds if the heat is high; keep the heat low, stir constantly and take the pan off for a moment if it looks curdled.

steps.title: Make the rice water
steps.text: While the masala simmers, bring 500 ml water to a boil in the saucepan with 1 bay leaf, 1 clove, 1 cardamom pod and 2 g salt.
steps.visualCue: A rolling boil and a sweet whole-spice smell
steps.videoShot: Whole spices floating in boiling water.
steps.watchOut: Too little water; the rice needs plenty of boiling water, so use the full 500 ml.

steps.title: Return the eggs
steps.text: Put the fried eggs into the masala, spoon some over them and turn the heat off.
steps.visualCue: Eggs coated in thick red masala, with a bed of masala under them
steps.videoShot: Eggs rolled in masala.
steps.watchOut: A watery base, which makes the rice soggy; if there is pooled water, cook the masala on medium for 1–2 min first.

steps.title: Boil the rice
steps.text: Drain the soaked rice, add it to the boiling water and cook about 5–6 min.
steps.visualCue: A grain pressed between two fingers breaks into pieces but still shows a thin white core
steps.cameraCheck: A grain pressed between two fingers
steps.videoShot: Rice drained into a sieve, steam rising.
steps.watchOut: Cooking the rice fully, which turns it to mush on dum; take a grain out at 5 min and drain as soon as it is about 75% cooked. If it overshoots, drain at once and spread it on a plate to stop the cooking.

steps.title: Drain the rice
steps.text: Pour the rice into a sieve, remove the whole spices and shake out the water.
steps.visualCue: Separate grains, no water running out
steps.videoShot: Rice shaken in a sieve.
steps.watchOut: Rice left sitting wet, which keeps cooking and clumps; drain well and layer straight away.

steps.title: Layer the rice
steps.text: Spread the drained rice evenly over the eggs and masala. Top with the mint and coriander, ¾ tsp (1.5 g) garam masala, 1 tsp (5 g) ghee and 1 tsp (5 ml) lemon juice.
steps.visualCue: A white rice layer with green herbs and a glossy ghee shine on top
steps.videoShot: Rice and herbs spooned over the masala.
steps.watchOut: Pressing the rice down, which squashes the grains; spoon it on lightly.

steps.title: Dum (seal and steam)
steps.text: Cover tightly. Put the pan on the tawa on the lowest heat and cook.
steps.tip: Don't lift the lid during dum; the steam is what finishes the rice.
steps.visualCue: Steam leaks only slightly at the lid edge and a roasted spice smell rises
steps.cameraCheck: The sealed pan on the tawa
steps.videoShot: A lid pressed down over the pan, steam at the edge.
steps.watchOut: A burning smell from the base, which means the heat is too high; switch off at once, and if it has caught, do not scrape the burnt layer into the dish.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Switch off the heat and leave the pan covered.
steps.visualCue: Steam stops pushing at the lid and the aroma settles
steps.videoShot: Lid kept on the resting pan.
steps.watchOut: Opening early, which lets the steam escape; wait the full 5 min.

steps.title: Mix and plate
steps.text: Gently fold from the bottom with a spoon and plate the rice with the 2 eggs on top.
steps.visualCue: Rice grains that are long, separate and fluffy, with orange streaks of masala; eggs whole
steps.videoShot: A spoon folding rice, then a slow pan over the plate.
steps.watchOut: Stirring hard, which breaks the grains and eggs; fold from the bottom up using a slow lifting motion.

reasons: a complete, filling one-pot meal with about 21 g of protein, B12, selenium and vitamin D from the eggs, no deep frying and measured fat. Points off for white basmati rice (low fibre, about 4 g), very high dietary cholesterol (about 390 mg from 2 eggs), saturated fat (about 9 g), and sodium of about 1,420 mg. Restaurant versions usually use more oil, ghee and salt, deep-fried onions and bigger rice portions.

researchRating.basis: egg biryani is a popular, easy and affordable biryani, with many recipe versions across Indian recipe sites (Ranveer Brar, Indian Healthy Recipes, My Ginger Garlic Kitchen, Piping Pot Curry, Sailu's Food, Onmanorama, Chetna Makan); points off because it is seen as a quick "everyday" biryani rather than the celebrated meat versions, and recipe review counts could not be viewed (search snippets only).

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 1 day (cool within 1 hour; eggs and rice are both high-risk if left out). Do not freeze (boiled-egg whites turn rubbery). Reheat only once, with 1 tbsp water, covered, until steaming hot all the way through (about 2 min in a microwave, stirring once).
leftoverRemix: Egg biryani fried-rice wrap. Chop the leftover eggs, stir-fry them with the rice and a little chopped onion for 2 min, and roll it in a roti or paratha with mint chutney. Eat the same day.
burnOff: about 8.7 km of running (610 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 12.2 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 25 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: contains egg, onion, garlic and table salt, all avoided in vrat

ekadashi.reason: contains rice, egg, onion and garlic, all avoided on Ekadashi

jain.reason: egg, onion, garlic and fresh ginger (root vegetables); this agrees with the ingredient list

ramadan.reason: eggs are halal and no meat is used; filling at about 21 g protein, but about 1,420 mg sodium (est.) can add to thirst, so cut the salt to 2 g for sehri

jain.reason: contains egg, onion, garlic and fresh ginger; Jain rules exclude all of them

pescatarian.reason: eggs and dairy only, no meat or fish (pescatarian diets usually include eggs and dairy)

sattvik.reason: contains onion and garlic, and egg

glutenFree.reason: rice-based and this recipe uses no hing (asafoetida); most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so check the garam masala label too

dairyFree.reason: curd 40 g → coconut yoghurt 40 g and ghee 5 g → oil 5 g
